subject.title: AI safety taxonomy: plugin-emitted detectors and evals

question: Should OpenClaw admit plugin-generated AI-safety events through a dedicated manifest-gated public SDK contract, and which provenance, privacy, cardinality, trust, and exporter rules must that contract enforce?
rationale: This creates a durable plugin API and determines whether untrusted plugin-emitted classifications can enter security-sensitive diagnostic and telemetry surfaces; source inspection cannot choose that policy safely.

options.title: Define schema and boundary first
options.body: Approve the core taxonomy, privacy rules, provenance model, and exporter limits before revising the linked implementation PR to match that contract.

options.title: Use generic diagnostics only
options.body: Extend the existing diagnostic event union and dispatcher without adding a separate safety-specific service-context or manifest API.

options.title: Keep detectors external
options.body: Do not add a new core SDK contract; let plugins retain and export detector results through their own storage or telemetry integrations.

recommendation.title: Define schema and boundary first
recommendation.body: Approve the core taxonomy, privacy rules, provenance model, and exporter limits before revising the linked implementation PR to match that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most directly connects this person to the diagnostic event dispatcher, exporters, and operator-facing diagnostics surfaces affected by the decision.
